about: More damage for conformance/ledger/cases.json. Each case gives the whole file as text (UTF-8) and what protocol/ledger.md says `ledger-read` must answer. Where the answer is corrupt, `ledger-append` must answer corrupt too and leave the file as it was. `unlisted_kind` is an entry of a kind no rule gives a meaning: it is appended through the kernel, kept by the reader, and an append after it works. `deepest` is an entry nested 64 levels deep, the most a ledger allows: it is appended through the kernel, and an append after it works. `bad_requests` are requests to `ledger-append`, given without the ledger's name, that must be answered {"refused": "bad-request"} with nothing written, whether the ledger is new, well formed, corrupt or locked; where `body_levels` is given, the request's `body` is an object nested that many levels deep, `{"x": {"x": ... {}}}`. Built with the reference encoder; no kernel produced any of it.

damage.name: a byte changed in the body of the last entry, the chain untouched
damage.note: The payload is still canonical and nothing follows it, so only the checksum can notice.

damage.name: a length that is not the payload's
damage.note: The checksum is right. Only the length is wrong.

damage.name: a length with a leading zero
a length with a plus sign
a checksum in uppercase
two spaces between fields
two spaces after the format marker only
two spaces after the length only
two spaces after the checksum only
damage.note: A reader that takes everything after the third space as the payload sees a payload that starts with a space: the length and the checksum no longer fit it.

damage.name: a tab in place of a space
a space after the payload
a byte-order mark before the first entry
a blank line between entries
a blank line at the end
a file that is one line feed
damage.note: An empty file has no entries. This one has a line, and the line is empty.

damage.name: the last entry written twice
damage.note: The repeated line names the entry before the last as its previous.

damage.name: an entry whose previous is the entry before the last
the first entry removed
damage.note: The first entry of a ledger has previous null.

damage.name: a later entry whose previous is null
an entry with a fourth field
an entry with no body
a payload that is null
a payload that is a list
an entry whose kind is not a string
another format marker
a final line ended by a carriage return alone
damage.note: There is no line feed after it, so it is a torn ending like any other.

damage.name: a well-formed entry of a kind the reader gives no meaning
damage.note: A reader keeps entries of every kind.

damage.name: an entry nested 64 levels deep
damage.note: The entry itself is the first level. 64 levels is the limit, and is read.

damage.name: an entry nested 65 levels deep
damage.note: Every reader must be able to read every entry: nesting deeper than 64, the entry itself counted, makes the line corrupt.

bad_requests.name: a body that would nest the entry 65 levels deep
a kind that is a number
